title: Agents & conversation — where it stands
eyebrow: Capability positioning · read from the source, not from memory
thesis: A deliberate inversion of LangChain and AutoGen. Where those are LLM-driven autonomy frameworks — the model picks tools, plans, and orchestrates — Softanza builds a governed, declarative substrate where an LLM only proposes and can never act. Agents are `.pia` files judged at load; they rehearse into a virtual-filesystem twin and only a committing actor writes reality, under three gates; a capability lattice makes "an LLM cannot act effectfully" a static, provable invariant. It is strongest exactly where the peers are weakest — safety, governance, determinism — and deliberately absent exactly where they lead: LLM-driven tool selection, autonomous planning, live multi-agent chat, and RAG.
grid_title: Twelve lanes, each against its category leader
grid_lede: Every lane names what actually ships, the tools it is fair to measure against, and the one thing still owed. Read the Partial/Emerging lanes carefully: several are capabilities Softanza refuses by design (LLM-driven action), not merely unbuilt.

lanes.engine: The differentiator: an agent (`stzAgentWorkbench`) rehearses file/system changes into a virtual-filesystem twin, then exports one governed `GenerateUpdatePlan()`. A separate committing actor executes it under three gates — scope, capability, governance — leaving an audit trail. "Build a safe world, and let ordinary agents loose inside it."
lanes.owed: Proven: a `Cycle()` fires, the disk does not move, the plan carries one op, an `LLMActor` cannot commit, only the in-scope actor makes it real. No mainstream framework has this — a genuine category-of-one.

lanes.engine: Agents compose as a colored `stzAgentGraph` where an `llm_actor` holds `[inference]` only. Five statically-proven invariants (no-llm-effectful, effects-guarded, open-text-contained, effects-traced, effects-dominated) feed the one CI gate, and `no-llm-effectful` is enforced at two doors — graph construction and engine registration — with the same sentence.
lanes.owed: A provable governance graph is far beyond the peers' runtime-only guardrails. The "effects-dominated" strengthening (every input→effect path crosses a guardian) is the newest rung.

lanes.engine: An agent is a file: a closed, versioned `.pia` declaration (kind, coverage, reversibility, schedule, skills, governance) — or a `.ring` program — judged at LOAD by a sequence of courts. A defect is a refusal in the unified finding shape, one per gate (14 refusal codes), before the agent ever runs.
lanes.owed: Declarative, governed, version-gated agents validated before execution — no peer validates an agent at load like this. A distinctive deployment model (drop a file in a folder, it mounts or is refused).

lanes.engine: `agentloop.zig` — Zig owns time, Ring runs `Cycle()`, and there is no callback into the Ring VM: the loop publishes a schedule (a run queue) rather than invoking. Total order is priority then registration; timer/event/mailbox/manual triggers; an over-full queue drops and counts; the loop states its own coverage at runtime.
lanes.owed: Determinism-as-a-test (same sequence → same order, twice) and 15 Zig unit tests. The engine pump is opt-in today — a stated migration state that flips when the last in-tree host declares.

lanes.engine: An `llm_actor` proposes through `stzLLMFunction` + `stzOutputSchema`: a declared structure, compiled to a GBNF grammar, enforced at the sampler so invalid tokens are unemittable. The proposal is validated against the declared shape and written to the agent's own memory — "a candidate, never an effect."
lanes.owed: Grammar-constrained decoding beats retry-based parsing — the deep rating lives on the Neural tier page; here it is the solid mechanism by which an LLM contributes without acting.

lanes.engine: `stzConversation` — a goal-driven "wise-coding" loop inside a `stzKnowledgeGraph`: it holds one accountable `stzGoal`, generates the next question from the goal's gaps, admits answers through governed `Admit`, checkpoints refusals, and persists as `.zcnv` — with optional neural rephrasing.
lanes.owed: A distinctive system-led, gap-born dialogue — but deterministic and narrower than a full dialogue manager (no intent classification, no free-form NLU beyond the answer registers).

lanes.engine: `stzAgentMemory` over a `stzKnowledgeGraph`: `Learn` / `Recall` / `Forget` / `Prove` over case-folded (subject, predicate, object) triples, persistable.
lanes.owed: Graph-backed, provable memory is a nice distinctive — but there is no conversation-buffer / summary / vector memory variety LangChain offers, and no automatic recency/relevance management.

lanes.engine: `stzLLMFunction`: typed returns (`ReturnsNumber/Boolean/OneOf/Structure`), a call budget, retries, goldens (`AddGolden/RunGoldens`), a template prompt with `{input}` substitution, and a real GGUF backend (`UseResponder` / `SeedAnswer` for model-free tests).
lanes.owed: A clean single-function abstraction with goldens — but no chain/pipeline ecosystem, and no prompt registry or versioning beyond the template. Narrower than LangChain's composition surface.

lanes.engine: `stzAgentGraph` composes roles (pi / llm / hybrid / guardian / effect / tool) with edges (`Proposes` / `Guards` / `Feeds` / `Escalates`) and proves soundness. An engine mailbox (`stz_agent_send_msg`) carries messages.
lanes.owed: Composition-as-proof is elegant, but there is no runtime multi-agent conversation orchestrator (AutoGen's core), the native roster is one-fifth wired, and `stzHybridAgent` exists only as a graph node, not a class.

lanes.engine: A skill's `ring:<Function>` clause binds a plain Ring function, governed by an execution `posture` (trusted / external / sandboxed) composed against the agent's reversibility class. Tools are `tool` nodes with `[compute]` capability.
lanes.owed: No LLM-driven tool selection — the defining feature of LangChain/AutoGen tool agents. Binding is declarative and posture-gated; which tool runs is decided by the deterministic agent, not the model. A deliberate refusal, but a gap against the peers.

lanes.engine: Deterministic perceive→decide→act to a fixpoint (`stzPIAgent.Pursue`, `RunToQuiet`), and gap-driven slot-filling via `stzGoal`.
lanes.owed: No LLM-driven planning — no ReAct, no stepwise / Handlebars planner. Reasoning is a deterministic fixpoint; the `planner` agent is reserved, not wired. Autonomous multi-step reasoning is the peers' headline and is absent here by design.

lanes.engine: Not wired into the agent tier. The nearest tie-in is `stzAgentMemory` over the knowledge graph; the semantic index (`stzSemanticIndex`, embeddings) lives on the Neural tier and is not connected to agent proposal or memory.
lanes.owed: Retrieval-augmented generation — a headline of every peer — is absent from agents. The embedding retrieval to build it already exists one tier over; it just isn't connected.

gaps_title: The gaps, ordered by return — not by size
gaps_lede: Three tiers. The first two add the peers' capabilities inside the governance frame (LLM proposes, a gate commits); the third finishes the owed negotiation and evaluation surfaces.

tiers.title: Tier A — the peers' strengths, governed

items.title: LLM-driven tool selection, gated
items.text: Let an `llm_actor` propose which tool to call (a ReAct-style loop), with a deterministic pi-gate approving the commit. This adds LangChain's core capability without surrendering the "LLM never acts" invariant — proposal, not authority.

items.title: Wire RAG into agents
items.text: Connect the existing `stzSemanticIndex` to agent memory and LLM proposals, so an agent can retrieve before it proposes. The retrieval engine ships one tier over; this is a wiring job with high visible return.

tiers.title: Tier B — finish the owed surfaces

items.title: Plan negotiation (Receive / Revise)
items.text: The agent's side of the plan handshake — `Receive(aIssues)` / `Revise()` — so a rejected update plan comes back for repair instead of just failing. Named as owed in the design doc.

items.title: Live multi-agent orchestration
items.text: A runtime message-passing / group-chat layer over the proven graph — turning static composition into live collaboration, the way AutoGen runs a conversation between agents.

items.title: Wire the roster & build stzHybridAgent
items.text: Four of five native agents are reserved and `stzHybridAgent` is only a graph node. Wiring them (and the hybrid class) turns the honest one-fifth roster into a working fleet.

items.title: stzAgentEvaluation — the examination hall
items.text: A structured harness to score an agent's proposals against expectations (beyond goldens on a single LLM function). Named as owed; the piece that makes agent quality measurable, not just governed.

items.title: Branch-per-hypothesis exploration
items.text: `BranchFrom` / `CompareBranches` — let an agent rehearse several futures in parallel workbenches and compare, using the safe-world twin that already exists. A natural, distinctive extension of the rehearse model.

items.title: Governed autonomous planning
items.text: An LLM planner that proposes a multi-step plan, re-validated and committed step-by-step under the three gates — the peers' autonomy, made auditable. The reserved `planner` agent's eventual home.

notes.lead: The honesty line on the ratings.
notes.text: This tier is heavily guarded and green — the agent loop (determinism proven as a test, the drop-and-count under overflow), the `.pia` court (one refusal per gate, every one at LOAD), and the safe world (the disk provably does not move until a scoped actor commits). Two caveats: the LLM-model-dependent paths run model-free in CI via `SeedAnswer`/`UseResponder`, so the governance is proven but proposal quality is not CI-tested; and `stzNarration` was renamed to `stzTranscript` (not a lost capability — the git delete/add pair is the rename).

Softanza's agents are the safest, most governable, most declarative of their field — a provably-contained substrate no LLM framework offers — and the deliberate cost of that is the autonomy the field is famous for: LLM-driven tool use, planning, live multi-agent chat and RAG are refused or unbuilt, and closing the gap means adding those as governed proposals rather than autonomous authority.
